title: Dual invariance of switching failure
statement: Let $f:\\{-1,1\\}^n\\to\\{-1,1\\}$ be a sign-valued Boolean function, let $\\delta\\in\\mathbb R$, and let $k\\in\\mathbb N$. Define its Boolean dual by $f^*(x)=-f(-x)$. The switching-failure probability at parameters $\\delta,k$ is unchanged by dualization: $P_{\\delta,k}(f^*)=P_{\\delta,k}(f)$, where $P_{\\delta,k}(f)$ is the weighted average over random restrictions of the indicator that the restricted function has decision-tree depth at least $k$.
hypotheses_covered: A Boolean function on the sign cube with sign-valued output
